examples.knowledge_point: Line Integrals of Unity With Respect to Y
examples.problem:
Calculate $\displaystyle\int_C \,\textrm d y,$ where $C$ is the path along the semicircle of radius $3,$ traversed from the point $(3,0)$ to the point $(-3,0),$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14059897/assets/ca97546ecaf9e37bee53fcc2b0c66962cff67a91ee9b117cc8ac8531efa23efc.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
\int_C \,\textrm d y = y_2 - y_1,
$$

where $y_2$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and $y_1$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, $y_2 = 0$ and $y_1 = 0.$ Therefore,

$$
\int_C \,\textrm d y = y_2 - y_1 =  0 - 0 = 0.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14059897/assets/eaf6f930e6e28f4574587880fefbcf336a0cd2a03d9c5bf347440227f31dbdf7.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path comprising of a horizontal line segment of length $2$ and a semicircle of radius $4,$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=-3$ and ${x}_{1}=7.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=(-3)-7=-10.
$$
